newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SHARES MIXED, GAS FIRM FALLS.
newsitem.headline: SHARES MIXED, GAS FIRM FALLS.

text.p: * Lithuanian share prices were mixed on Tuesday, with 15 of the 43 stocks on the A list easing, eight rising and the rest holding firm or trading in a range above and below their price on Monday.
* Lithuanian Gas returned to the market after a suspension because of its shareholders' meeting and promptly lost nine percent, falling to 1.82 litas from 2.00 litas.
* Vilniaus Bank eased to 221.00 litas from 235.00 litas while Siauliu Bank sank for the third straight session, falling to 82.00 litas from 90.00 litas.
Lithuanian shares were mixed on Tuesday and the short-term outlook was gloomy, dealers said.

"We only have local investors right now and a few orders from the Nordic countries...the big investors are still examining the market and haven't come yet," said Kestutis Kupsys, a dealer with brokerage house Mendes Prior Europe.
"Instead of using the central market, big foreign investors have been opting for block trades and direct purchases," he added.
The session's losers included Vilniaus Bank, which eased to 221.00 litas from 235.00 litas.
Siauliu Bank stumbled for the third straight session after rising steeply last week on news that Hermis Bank planned to buy 51 percent of its shares.
Dealers said its price had risen too high too fast last week.
"Its price increase was purely speculative and fueled by investors who did not examine the situation carefully," said Arvydas Jacikevicius of brokerage firm Suprema.
"Just because the central bank gave Hermis Bank permission to acquire 51 percent of Siauliu Bank's shares doesn't mean that it will happen...and there is a chance that it won't happen," he said.
Lithuanian Gas lost nine percent on its first day of trade after a suspension because of its shareholders' meeting on Monday.
The company reported a loss of 15.975 million litas but dealers said that it had lots of room to move up as its long-term prospects are good and its price looks like a bargain at the moment.
